Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Most expensive UGEL hostel costs GH¢8,000 per academic year – CEO Source : Albert Kuzor 18 November 2026 8:55am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Chief Executive Officer of the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL), Yawo Agbesi, has defended accommodation charges at the university’s hostels, saying the most expensive facility, excluding the Graduate Hostel, costs GH¢8,000 per academic year.
This means that for the four students who share a room, GH¢8,000 per student comes to GH¢ 32,000.
He said the amount, spread across two 16-week semesters, translates into an average of about GH¢35 per day.
Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Wednesday, November 18, Mr Agbesi said the fee covers essential services, including electricity, water, maintenance and cleaning.
"For our facility, the most expensive, as we speak now, apart from the graduate hostel, is roughly about GH¢8,000 a year, that is for the full year. If you look at the GH¢8,000 as we speak, that means 16 weeks per semester, two semesters, that is 32 weeks, that is one academic year; that means if we divide that GH¢8,000 by 32, we are looking at an average of every student paying GH¢35 per day," he said.
"Electricity, they don't pay; sometimes they come in, and for the whole semester the lights don't go off. It also includes water, which they don't pay for. We do maintenance facilities; we provide cleaning services as well for the students," he added.
Mr Agbesi acknowledged concerns about the conditions of some hostel facilities but said management was addressing the challenges in phases.
He said UGEL was aware of complaints raised by students and remained committed to improving the facilities to enhance their accommodation experience.
He also urged students to use the appropriate grievance channels to report their concerns, saying this would enable management to respond and address the issues effectively.
His comments follow a confrontation between Acting Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku and a hostel manager during an inspection of UGEL hostels on the University of Ghana campus.
A video of the encounter, which nearly escalated into a physical altercation, went viral on social media, triggering renewed public debate about hostel management, accommodation charges and the condition of facilities on the campus.
The incident has also brought renewed attention to students’ concerns about the quality of hostel accommodation and calls for improved oversight of the facilities.
